questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics' refers to.
questions.a: Microeconomics focuses on individual decision-makers and specific markets, whereas macroeconomics analyzes aggregate indicators and the behavior of the economy as a whole.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics'.
questions.a: Microeconomics studies individual choices, while macroeconomics studies aggregate economic phenomena.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction (source: leec101.txt lines 10-120)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic Agents' refers to.
questions.a: Individuals or institutional entities that make decisions regarding consumption, production, taxation, and financial transactions in an economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic Agents'.
questions.a: Decision-makers in an economy, ranging from consumers to state institutions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Economic Agents' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Economic Agents (source: leec101.txt lines 121-135)

questions.q: Calculate the unemployment rate given the number of employed and unemployed people.. Use the method 'Unemployment Rate'. Work with: employed = 360, unemployed_looking = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployment_rate.
questions.a: 0.0137 per cent

questions.q: Find the rate of unemployment when some are working and others are looking for jobs.. Use the method 'Unemployment Rate'. Work with: employed = 8, unemployed_looking = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployment_rate.
questions.a: 0.2727 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unemployment Rate' refers to.
questions.a: The proportion of the active labor force that is currently without work but actively seeking employment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unemployment Rate'.
questions.a: Measures the share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Unemployment Rate', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: unemployment_rate = unemployed_looking / (employed + unemployed_looking)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Characteristics of a Capitalist Economy' refers to.
questions.a: An economic system characterized by private ownership of production means, production aimed at market sale, and the employment of wage labor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Characteristics of a Capitalist Economy'.
questions.a: Private ownership, market-oriented production, and wage labor define capitalism.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Characteristics of a Capitalist Economy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.2 (source: leec101.txt lines 245-290)

questions.q: Calculate the profit of a firm given its revenue, rent, interest, and wages.. Use the method 'Profit of a Capitalist Firm'. Work with: interest = 18, rent = 80, revenue = 20000, wages = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit.
questions.a: 19402 rupees

questions.q: Find the entrepreneur's profit when revenue, rent, interest, and wages are known.. Use the method 'Profit of a Capitalist Firm'. Work with: interest = 18, rent = 120, revenue = 80000, wages = 1000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit.
questions.a: 78862 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Profit of a Capitalist Firm' refers to.
questions.a: The residual revenue retained by an entrepreneur after paying rent for land, interest for capital, and wages for labor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Profit of a Capitalist Firm'.
questions.a: Profit is the remaining revenue after all factor payments are deducted.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Profit of a Capitalist Firm', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: profit = revenue - rent - interest - wages

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Four Sectors of the Economy' refers to.
questions.a: The macroeconomic classification of an economy into households, firms, government, and the external sector.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Four Sectors of the Economy'.
questions.a: The economy is composed of households, firms, government, and the rest of the world.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Four Sectors of the Economy' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Calculate the net exports of an economy.. Use the method 'Net Exports'. Work with: exports = 30, imports = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_exports.
questions.a: -50 rupees

questions.q: Find the trade balance given exports and imports.. Use the method 'Net Exports'. Work with: exports = 80, imports = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_exports.
questions.a: -220 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Net Exports' refers to.
questions.a: The difference between the value of goods and services sold to foreign countries and those purchased from them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Net Exports'.
questions.a: Net balance of trade with the external sector.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Net Exports', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: net_exports = exports - imports
